packets.title: Temperature-qualified material work
packets.purpose: Make one original workshop process use its actual batch condition, fuel and output, so ordinary material preparation remains useful.
packets.player_choice: Warm a cold owned batch now, spend less fuel after shelter conditioning, or choose a useful lower-temperature process.
packets.scope: One optional Frontier workshop process with one actual input batch, two supported approaches and useful output/residue. Add a typed per-batch condition only if existing item metadata cannot represent it. No global thermal grid.
packets.integration_need: Root-owned exact item/state validation and batch metadata, stable definition/version, material reserve, process completion and native output publication. Current finite crop and stamped strip retain their meanings.

decision_chain.requires: Known process, owned unencumbered material, usable hands/site and actual disclosed fuel
decision_chain.reserve: Exact batch and fuel from their owners; freeze initial condition/recipe revision
decision_chain.outcome: Consume the reserved batch once and produce exact useful output plus disclosed residue
decision_chain.consumer: Later repair/cooking/insulation job must use that produced material function
decision_chain.failure: Cancel/lose support follows declared frozen return policy; completed heating is not retroactively refunded
decision_chain.aftermath: Retain input/output/temperature-basis receipt and changed site condition

packets.time_policy: Existing played clock and supported absence policy; no browser-closed heating/loss.
packets.compatibility: Additive optional typed record with explicit version validation; old absence inert. Do not infer arbitrary fields are accepted by existing item validators.
packets.later_acceptance: UI shows actual costs and batch basis; warmer input changes the authored cost; later consumer spends the produced item; cancellation, storage, transfer and generated save/reload prove custody.
packets.risks: Per-batch metadata is shared integration work; simplified source heating is not physical science or selected balance.
packets.check_policy: syntax/import/definition/link/build useful during current phase; unit/browser/gameplay/save/failure/regression acceptance deferred until authorized

packets.title: Body-specific expedition support
packets.purpose: Let a short original flooded or stale-air task distinguish learned movement, actual air support and current body requirements.
packets.player_choice: Use an actual breathing/lining kit, take a reachable recovery route, or use an already-earned supported alternative body where its own sustain law allows.
packets.scope: One explicitly enrolled local hazard with warning, voluntary retreat and useful result. No automatic body grant, copied bionic lore, world reset or mandatory fatal/offline upkeep.
packets.integration_need: Actual current body/function owner and kit/air reserve, supported action adapter, warning/recovery state and completion support. Traveler profiles alone are detached snapshots, not a new native physiology engine.

decision_chain.requires: Actual supported body, learned route/movement function, known hazard and sufficient support
decision_chain.reserve: Owned physical kit/reserve and real attention, not a capability label
decision_chain.transition: Played-time local exposure with a defined safe-recovery window
decision_chain.outcome: Useful work consumes support; deficient support pauses/forces a disclosed retreat
decision_chain.consumer: Same body can resume only after actual recovery/refill or alternate practical approach
decision_chain.failure: Unsupported body, expired support or unreachable recovery prevents completion; no invented source immunity
decision_chain.aftermath: Received observations, support spent and recovery retained separately

packets.time_policy: One existing clock; unobserved/absent region freezes unless its current owner explicitly supports the hazard.
packets.compatibility: Optional new content/version records; existing normal bodies and care jobs unchanged. Schema/validation and generated save/reload gate before verified claim.
packets.later_acceptance: Movement learning unlocks a concrete path but does not conjure air; different supported bodies pay their declared resources; warning/retreat/resume and exact kit custody are visible.
packets.risks: Body support integration is broader than a label; fatality and autonomous hazard policies are not selected.
packets.check_policy: syntax/import/definition/link/build useful during current phase; unit/browser/gameplay/save/failure/regression acceptance deferred until authorized

packets.title: Borrowed competence with earned practice
packets.purpose: Make a powered borrowed workshop tool enable a specific operation while keeping learned mastery, rental rights and fuel distinct.
packets.player_choice: Borrow and power the tool for a difficult joint, do an ordinary slower task, or practice toward retaining the skill without it.
packets.scope: One existing workshop action and one specific removable tool support. No global skill-slot cap or blanket XP/morale system.
packets.integration_need: Separate tool-owned derived execution contribution, actual lease/equipment custody and earned practice ledger; integrate with one native command without duplicating source/perk effects.

decision_chain.requires: Current tool rights/installed support, site, usable body and real funded power
decision_chain.reserve: Borrowed item custody/deposit, owner energy and real work attention
decision_chain.transition: Tool-enabled work or slower ordinary practice on existing clock
decision_chain.outcome: Tool contribution enables execution; actual earned practice is recorded only from qualified completed work
decision_chain.consumer: A later action without the tool tests retained learned capability
decision_chain.failure: Tool return, support loss or exhausted power removes only tool contribution; cancellation follows actual lease/job policy
decision_chain.aftermath: Returned custody and conserved deposit; lasting learned practice survives removal

packets.time_policy: Existing work job and energy owner; no render-triggered rewards, passive duplicate drain or new timer.
packets.compatibility: Do not copy ONI UngrantSkill behavior: equipment removal must not delete separately earned skill history. Additive definition/custody validation and explicit effect stacking.
packets.later_acceptance: Borrowed tool enables the named operation; power is spent once; tool removal disables only its contribution; later learned competence still works after return and generated reload.
packets.risks: Derived capability/equipment integration must avoid double bonuses and aliases; aptitude or consent cannot be inferred from tool ownership.
packets.check_policy: syntax/import/definition/link/build useful during current phase; unit/browser/gameplay/save/failure/regression acceptance deferred until authorized

packets.title: Paid habitat and useful biological output
packets.purpose: Add one optional original husbandry loop whose supported habitat and consumed feed affect a useful harvest/byproduct.
packets.player_choice: Maintain a cultivated habitat for reliable production, use a slower wild-compatible approach, or deliberately end the tended cycle and keep remaining means.
packets.scope: One newly authored optional bed or small husbandry site, separate from Nell's existing finite crop. Explicit renewal spends actual new inputs. No free reseeding, population ecology or unearned companion.
packets.integration_need: Existing stock/site/job owner with a named lifecycle phase, habitat support and owned feed/renewal input. Define whether feed alternatives are OR or jointly required.

decision_chain.requires: Actual site rights, current habitat, known species/process and owned inputs
decision_chain.reserve: Feed/seed-equivalent/care materials and real responsible worker
decision_chain.transition: Supported tending/growth phase; unsuitable habitat stalls according to explicit rule
decision_chain.outcome: Create a real counted product and qualified byproduct; current cycle ends once
decision_chain.consumer: Cooking, refining or medical-fiction preparation spends the produced stock
decision_chain.failure: Insufficient support stalls without invented death; interruption preserves declared phase/input policy
decision_chain.aftermath: Spent means, current site and cycle result remain; new cycle requires explicit renewal

packets.time_policy: Supported played-time lease only; preserve old finite-crop and unsupported body/absence freeze policies.
packets.compatibility: Separate stable content IDs and optional lifecycle record; old story receipts/rewards cannot be replayed.
packets.later_acceptance: Feeding actual owned stock changes output availability; unsupported habitat blocks growth; useful output reaches a later native consumer; renewal cannot farm free stock or rewrite old crop.
packets.risks: New lifecycle content needs authoring and exact stock conservation; source wild/tame/fertility policies are examples, not universal YAIR ecology rules.
packets.check_policy: syntax/import/definition/link/build useful during current phase; unit/browser/gameplay/save/failure/regression acceptance deferred until authorized

packets.title: One operator, two work locations
packets.purpose: Prototype original remote operation that uses one actual operator and a supported remote device rather than duplicate independent labor.
packets.player_choice: Operate a remote device while staying sheltered, send a willing independent worker with funded means, or travel and do the work personally.
packets.scope: One existing site and one bounded remote-control job. No mind duplication, free offline factory, native singleton copied world or global automation engine.
packets.integration_need: Root-owned binding of operator attention, device body/location/support, actual energy/cargo custody and job participants. Detached profiles must be joined through existing native adapters before claiming playable remote work.

decision_chain.requires: Known usable endpoint, actual controller/device permission and compatible control method
decision_chain.reserve: The real operator, device support, finite energy and exact target stock
decision_chain.transition: One supported control session/job, with any endpoint interruption observed by declared policy
decision_chain.outcome: Useful remote site output remains at its actual owner until collected/transferred
decision_chain.consumer: Later local use requires real collection/cargo/return rather than teleporting item creation
decision_chain.failure: Lost controller, exhausted fuel or inaccessible endpoint pauses/ends the job by explicit policy; no second person continues as the same mind
decision_chain.aftermath: Retain remote work result, operator occupation, remaining stock and changed return

packets.time_policy: Existing played clock and independent region leases; explicit pause/absence policy with no extra world clock.
packets.compatibility: One versioned job/context extension if necessary; unsupported old bodies/regions stay inert. Preserve a single attention/inventory/publisher owner.
packets.later_acceptance: Operator cannot perform incompatible simultaneous work; remote result stays in target custody; lost support stops useful work; personal/independent-worker alternatives remain distinct and generated reload retains the commitment.
packets.risks: This is the broadest packet and should follow an agreed shared interface; source terminal/depot internals and whole offscreen simulation remain incomplete.
packets.check_policy: syntax/import/definition/link/build useful during current phase; unit/browser/gameplay/save/failure/regression acceptance deferred until authorized
